accessibility.text: Example-Utilizing historical patient records with known outcomes (labels) to predict health outcomes.
© Zahra Shakeri, Dalla Lana School of Public Health, University of Toronto
A computer learns through trial and error, receiving feedback for its actions to optimize outcomes over time.
Letting a computer sift through patient data to find clusters of similar symptoms without any prior labeling.
Training a computer using labeled data, where the outcome is already known.
Allowing a computer to analyze data without explicit guidance, looking for patterns or structures.
A computer testing different public health strategies and adapting based on the success of each strategy, like improving vaccination campaigns based on feedback.
